cur:manuscripts-sinope-feeding-four-thou.summary: Beneath large gold uncial letters, Christ stands in a gold mantle between two apostles who hold out loaves and fishes, blessing the food; beside them lie great wicker baskets of bread, and the crowd sits in rows on a green hillside. At each side a haloed prophet leans over a framed panel bearing his prophecy. The miracle is shown as a sign of the Eucharist and of God's abundant care.
facts: Only 44 leaves of this purple Gospel book survive; it was bought at Sinope on the Black Sea in 1899 by a French officer and is now almost entirely in the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
Scientific analysis found that the purple of the parchment comes from orchil, a lichen dye, rather than the costly Tyrian purple, and that ultramarine blue was used in the painting.

cur:monumental-san-woman-issue-of-blood.summary: A woman kneels at Christ's feet and reaches for the hem of his garment, while the haloed Christ turns and gestures towards her; an apostle stands behind him and a group of onlookers waits at the right. The scene captures the moment the woman who had suffered for twelve years is healed by her faith.
facts: The thirteen scenes of the north wall show Christ's miracles and teaching; in all of them he appears young and beardless, robed in imperial purple.
The scenes were not arranged in biblical order but are thought to follow the Gospel readings of the Lenten liturgy in Theodoric's palace church.

cur:monumental-san-woman-issue-of-blood.notes: The Commons file name calls this 'noli me tangere', but the image shows the healing of the woman with an issue of blood, as the Commons category records.

cur:monumental-sma-adoration-of-magi.summary: Within a painted frame on a dark blue ground, the Magi in colourful robes approach from the left with their gifts towards the Virgin and Child, who are enthroned at the right. The panel belongs to a narrative cycle of the life of Christ painted in the church under Pope John VII; despite heavy losses, the procession of the Magi remains legible.
facts: Santa Maria Antiqua in the Roman Forum preserves wall paintings from the 6th to the late 8th century; buried after an earthquake in 847, it was rediscovered only in 1900.
Pope John VII (705–707) used Santa Maria Antiqua as his seat and had much of the church redecorated; most of the surviving paintings date from his time.

wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/4nuovo/2s.summary: On a gold ground above a flowering meadow, a bearded Christ in imperial purple sits on a jewelled throne with a red cushion, raising his right hand in blessing and holding a sceptre. Four angels in white, with haloes and long staffs, stand two by two on either side like a heavenly court. Christ appears here as King of Heaven, toward whom the procession of martyrs along the wall below advances.
facts: The group stands at the end of the south (right) wall, where a procession of 26 martyrs led by St Martin moves from Theodoric's palace toward the enthroned Christ; facing it on the north wall the Virgin and Child sit enthroned among four angels.
The church was built by the Ostrogothic king Theodoric as his palace church and dedicated in 504 to Christ the Redeemer.
The mosaics were restored in the mid-19th century by Felice Kibel.
wga:zearly/1/4mosaics/2ravenna/4nuovo/2s.notes: WGA dates it c. 500; the processions of martyrs on the same wall belong to the later, post-Arian redecoration of the 560s, the date of the enthroned Christ group itself was not independently confirmed. The mosaics were restored in the 19th century.
